title: This Cave Has Been Breathing Since 1881
note: Producer shot list (one shot per voice line) for audio/build_mix.py. The Animator may split shots; keep word counts.

shots.text: In 1881, two brothers in South Dakota heard a whistle coming from the ground.
They found a small hole in the rock. And the hole was breathing.
Wind rushed out so hard it blew Tom Bingham's hat off.
The obvious answer: a tunnel, with another opening somewhere.
But no other entrance was ever found. Just one hole, smaller than a sheet of paper.
Clue one. Later, the hole breathed in. It sucked Jesse's hat inside.
Clue two. It follows the weather. Before a storm, it blows out. In fair weather, it pulls in.
Clue three. Behind the hole is a maze: over two hundred and sixty kilometres of tunnels, still not fully explored.
So what makes a hole in the ground breathe?
The air above us is heavy. It presses on everything.
When a storm comes, that pressure drops, so the cave's air pushes harder and rushes out.
When the storm passes, the pressure rises, and the sky pushes air back in.
With that many tunnels, a tiny change moves a huge amount of air through one small hole.
Like a bag of chips on a plane, puffing up as the air outside thins.
The cave isn't breathing. The sky is.
And whenever a storm rolls over those hills, the little hole still breathes out, just like in 1881.
